Deposits at every FDIC-insured bank are.why: The $250,000 limit is the best-known fact about US deposit insurance; banks print it on their websites and statements.

Deposits at Dollar Bank are insured up t.why: The bank is named with its products, not with the federal limit. Exact forms of the direct statement are absent or nearly so; the only hit for 'Dollar Bank is insured' is one advertising page (indexed twice) reading 'Each depositor at Dollar Bank is insured to $250,000 by the FDIC', against 14,583 mentions of the bank. The AND hits for 'Dollar Bank AND FDIC' read are account advertisements without the limit. Common sense: people say 'deposits at FDIC-insured banks are insured up to $250,000' and that a given bank is FDIC-insured; nobody states the limit for one particular bank on its own, though it is true.

notes: Dev-split TBox revision on deposit_insurance_limit (new, staging/finance.RELATIONS.md): the class rule that every FDIC-insured bank's deposits are insured up to $250,000 per depositor, raised to $500,000. The real limit applies per depositor, per bank and per ownership category, so every question that asks the limit names a single-ownership account (the direct, paraphrase, cross-lingual and derived prompts), and the category rule never gives a second fair answer. The rule has held since 2010 (it was raised from $100,000 in 2008 and made permanent in 2010), and every member follows it, so there is no real exception. The derived queries name small banks the models are unlikely to know anything about by name (Dollar Bank, Bank of Clarke County, Farmers & Merchants Bank of Long Beach), give their FDIC membership in the prompt and ask the limit, the third as an application with arithmetic (the uninsured part of $600,000). Emigrant Bank was replaced because its own advertising states its $250,000 coverage, a member-specific route back to the old answer; Dollar Bank has one such page, recorded in its evidence. Unrelated near asks the credit-union counterpart's limit (NCUA, $250,000), the fact an over-applied edit would most likely leak into; its answer differs from the new $500,000 (Rule 7). The bank-in-prompt facts are true: all three are FDIC-insured US banks.
